content.thinking:
I need to plan out the module carefully, identifying the right imports for the builder, path, math, paint, and texture utilities before designing the fox stand concept.

For the actual fox geometry, I'm thinking through a kitsune standing pose facing forward, with nine fanning tails swept as tapered catmull paths with glowing flame tips, plus floating hitodama spirit orbs with flame shapes around it. I need to sketch out torso, leg, head, snout, and ear construction using sweeps and extrusions, placing eye decals carefully on the skull surface with safe null handling, then move into defining the cel-shaded paint palette.

Now I'm defining the coat color as a warm cream with crimson markings, using nested paint functions for sock-pattern coloring based on height, then working out the angular spread and curving path math for the nine tails fanning upward from the base like a peacock display.

I'm shading each tail with a gradient blending cream into red toward the tip, wrapped through the cel function for cohesive lighting, and making sure the tails arc upward so they never touch the ground near the paws. Each of the nine tails gets its own distinct paint, and I'm adding a small glowing teardrop flame extrusion at each tip for a spirit-fire effect.

Now I'm designing the flame shape as a crossed double-extrusion so it reads properly from any angle, and considering adding floating hitodama orbs with flame tails circling the fox at chest height, while keeping everything clear of the floor.

Still building the collar details...

For the back markings, I'll use a paint function tied to position and normal to generate red stripe bands across the upper back, checking z-position against a modular band width to create periodic stripes only where the surface faces upward.

Now I'm defining the belly as cream where the normal faces downward, then moving to the ears: shaping them as extruded triangular outlines positioned on the head with a width-aligned x-axis and slight lean, adding bevel and thickness, then placing a darker inner-ear shape offset slightly along the thickness axis to sit just above the outer ear surface.

I'm sketching the skull as a scaled sphere, sweeping the snout forward and down with a tapering radius, and adding a dark nose sphere at the tip. For the cheeks I'm placing small outward spikes on each side, and positioning eye decals symmetrically around the head's forward axis at a slight upward angle, making sure the decal scale looks proportionate.

For fur detail, I'm scattering cone-shaped spikes across the chest and neck using surface scatter rather than textured cards, translating each cone geometry so its base sits flush against the body surface instead of floating. I'm also setting up the torso as a swept surface shape to attach these elements onto.

Now I'm working out the leg geometry: front legs as thin tapered sweeps from shoulder to paw with shrinking radius values, using a color paint function that darkens the lower portion into sock-like markings. Hind legs follow a similar catmull-rom path through haunch, knee, and ankle points, with ellipsoid paws capping each limb.

I'm also checking vertical placement so the paw spheres and leg caps sit right at floor level without sinking below zero, then moving on to the torso and chest shapes defined by a smooth path with varying radii, followed by the start of a neck sweep rising from the chest into the head region.

Checking overall proportions next—ears and tails extending near the top of the figure, torso staying well above ground level, and the tail base overlapping the hips correctly. I'm also considering adding small gold ornaments like hoop earrings using tiny torus shapes on the ears.

Now I'm positioning anklet rings around each front leg using small flattened torus shapes aligned to the leg's path at specific points, oriented horizontally. I'm also thinking about adding hovering spirit flame orbs and maybe a glowing seal ring on the ground for extra magical detail.

For the floor, I'm adding a glowing magic circle decal facing upward, sized around 2.2m, positioned just above the ground to avoid clipping. I'm designing the circle's texture with cyan runes, a star, and concentric rings on a transparent background at 512 resolution.

Now I'm writing a flame helper for the spirit effect — crossed extruded shapes forming an outer cyan flame and a smaller inner white-blue one, both glowing, positioned at the tail tip and scaled per instance. I need to be careful with imports to avoid unused-name errors since there are many helper modules in play.

I'm planning out the tail flames and floating orbs — nine tails each with a few flame extrudes, plus seven orbs each pairing a sphere with two flames. For the tails themselves, I'm adding a color gradient from cream to red near the tip before the flame, and considering gold ring bands using a torus oriented along the tail's tangent direction at a point near the base.

I'm also adding a decal for a forehead mark on the head mesh, positioned near the top front. Writing the paint functions now...
